findings.label: Digital anomalies of hands and feet
findings.evidence: digitalization of the thumbs and shortening of the fifth finger of the right hand

panels.rationale: Single frontal clinical photograph of a patient from an article specifically on mosaic trisomy 8, showing linear truncal pigmentation and captioned digital/hand anomalies consistent with the disease.
panels.attribution_text: Giraldo et al. Mosaic trisomy 8 detected by fibroblasts cultured of skin.. Colombia medica (Cali, Colombia) 2016. doi:10.25100/cm.v47i2.2258. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Frontal view of patient in which linear blotches (in the thorax and abdomen) and alterations of the extremities can be observed (digitalization of the thumbs and shortening of the fifth finger of the right hand).
in_text_mentions: al examination revealed facial defects such as palpebral ptosis, small corneas and corectopia, hypoplasia of the upper maxilla and prognathism, dental crowding, high-arched palate, anomalies of the extremities such as digitalization of the thumbs, clinodactyly and bilateral shortening of the fifth finger, deep furrows in the palms and soles of the feet, shortening of the right femur and scoliosis. The skin presented brown linear blotches that followed Blaschko's lines which may reflect an embryological development (Fig. 1 and 2). We didn't have access to histological results of biopsy of skin.

panels.rationale: Clinical photograph of the soles of both feet showing deep plantar creases, explicitly captioned as characteristic in a case report of Warkany syndrome (mosaic trisomy 8). The finding matches the configured vocabulary entry for deep palmar/plantar creases. Skin tone not reliably assessable in this grayscale-converted, low-contrast image; age not stated in caption or in-text excerpt.
panels.attribution_text: Agrawal and Agrawal. Warkany syndrome: a rare case report.. Case reports in pediatrics 2011. doi:10.1155/2011/437101. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
in_text_mentions: rphic facial features included prominent forehead, large prominent ears with prominent antihelices, deep-set eyes, hypertelorism, bilateral corneal opacities, broad nose, thick everted lips, and high-arched palate. Orthopedic anomalies included camptodactyly of second through fifth fingers, mild scoliosis, short metatarsals, and deep plantar and deep palmar creases (Figure 1). X-ray spine showed mild scoliosis and posterior open neural arch defect in upper dorsal vertebra. Abdominal ultrasound, echocardiography, and cranial neuroimaging did not reveal any congenital anomaly of internal organs.
